title: The other player’s mix
hook: A toy rival changes its action mix. What happens to the same response’s expected payoff?

knows: basic arithmetic and the meaning of a percentage
doesNotKnow: Recompute a fixed response under a changed opponent mix while holding its conditional payoffs fixed.

misconception: A response’s payoff can be ranked without specifying what the other player does.
objective: Recompute a fixed response under a changed opponent mix while holding its conditional payoffs fixed.

claims.text: The Art of Strategy analyzes choices whose payoffs depend on other people’s choices.
claims.source: Avinash K. Dixit and Barry J. Nalebuff, The Art of Strategy (2008); chapter (unconfirmed); edition and bibliography not independently opened. Access hold F1.

claims.text: Original stipulated payoff model: A inputs [50, 8, -2] yield 3; B inputs [80, 8, -2] yield 6. Prediction correct option 6. A pays {A}; B pays {B}. The response itself is unchanged; the rival’s probability of choosing X rises from 50% to 80%. The rival mix is prescribed; no equilibrium, commitment or strategic adaptation is computed.
claims.source: Original lesson construction; EDD-010 formula ; exact independent Python arithmetic recomputation recorded in answerCheck; no book dataset or measured human response.

claims.text: A toy response pays 6 against X and −4 against Y; X occurs with probability 70%. Expected payoff? 0.7 × 6 + 0.3 × (−4) = 3; the same response could rank differently against another mix.
claims.source: Original transfer toy, payoff, inputs [70, 6, -4], output 3; independent Python recomputation.
